description: Samarium is a moderately hard silvery metal with symbol Sm and atomic number 62 that slowly oxidizes in air. As a typical lanthanide series member, it usually has an oxidation state of +3, though samarium(II) compounds are also known.
uses: The main commercial use is in samarium-cobalt magnets for permanent magnetization. Samarium-153 is used in the drug lexidronam to treat cancer, while samarium-149 is added to nuclear reactor control rods as a neutron absorber. Other applications include catalysis, radioactive dating, X-ray lasers, and samarium(II) iodide as a reducing agent in chemical synthesis.
characteristics: Samarium has hardness and density similar to zinc with a boiling point of 1,794 °C, making it the third most volatile lanthanide. It has one of the largest atomic radii among elements at 238 pm and exhibits paramagnetism at room temperature. The metal slowly oxidizes in air at room temperature and spontaneously ignites at 150 °C.
